## Why visit

A characterful rock pub in the hollow below Oxford Road station, with a tiled exterior and plenty of corners in which to sit. It offers a useful change of atmosphere on the Peveril–Britons–Oxford Road circuit, especially if music culture is part of the appeal of Manchester. The cask range is the beer reason to include it, and pizza can provide a straightforward food break. Expect a working music-oriented pub rather than a quiet preserved interior; timing around gigs will strongly affect the experience.

## Beer

CAMRA documents up to six real ales and notes a traditional strong ale among the selection; ask what is actually on. Theakston Old Peculier appears frequently in its CAMRA record; recent sightings include Millstone Stout. These are leads rather than a fixed beer list.

## Plan the visit

Card only in CAMRA’s listing. Gig-night crowds and the rock soundtrack are part of the appeal, but choose another room if quiet conversation is the priority.

**Getting there:** Immediately around Oxford Road station; combine with Lass O’Gowrie and Peveril of the Peak.

Check [November transport issues](../logistics.md) for date-specific disruption.
